harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a router between lan-a (node2, 10.10.1.0/24 via eth1) and lan-b (node3, 10.10.2.0/24 via eth2), with static addressing, per-subnet routes on node2/node3 pointing at node1, and a permissive forward filter — no NAT, so original source addresses are preserved. Verified bidirectional ping and TCP connectivity, and confirmed via tcpdump on node1's lan-b interface that node2's real 10.10.1.10 source address reaches node3 unmodified. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (VyOS reboot on node1, Alpine reboot on node2/node3), each proven via a changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id, with config persistence and cross-subnet connectivity re-verified after each recovery.
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 interfaces, OS, and existing config
Configured VyOS node1: eth1=10.10.1.254/24 (lan-a), eth2=10.10.2.254/24 (lan-b), firewall ipv4 forward filter default-action accept; committed and saved
Configured node2 /etc/network/interfaces: eth1=10.10.1.10/24 plus static route to 10.10.2.0/24 via 10.10.1.254
Configured node3 /etc/network/interfaces: eth1=10.10.2.10/24 plus static route to 10.10.1.0/24 via 10.10.2.254
Verified ping and TCP (nc) connectivity node2<->node3 through node1
Captured tcpdump on node1 eth2 during a node2->node3 TCP session and confirmed source IP 10.10.1.10 preserved (no NAT)
Captured boot_id baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via 'reboot', polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and persisted VyOS config + working routing
Restarted node2 via 'reboot', polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and persisted network config + working routing
Restarted node3 via 'reboot', polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and persisted network config + working routing

evidence.requirement: node1 configured to route between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3) with original source addresses preserved
evidence.summary: VyOS interfaces eth1/eth2 configured and committed; node2 pings node3 across the router; tcpdump on node1's lan-b interface shows the TCP SYN from node2 arriving with unmodified source 10.10.1.10 (no NAT), proving direct reachability with preserved source addresses.
Arbitrary TCP port (5001/5002) nc session from node2 to node3 succeeded and delivered payload, showing forwarding works for arbitrary ports, not just a hardcoded rule.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart persistence (boot identity change + recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id ebd78841...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 428d4ad0... confirms restart; VyOS config.boot shows persisted eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding still enabled; ping node2->node3 succeeds post-reboot.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart persistence (boot identity change + recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a8b262d7...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id cbcb28f7... confirms restart; /etc/network/interfaces persisted the eth1 static IP and route hook, ping to node3 succeeds post-reboot.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart persistence (boot identity change + recovery)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id b77dad80...; reboot acknowledged; new boot_id 5906fe4a... confirms restart; eth1 static IP and route persisted, ping to node2 succeeds post-reboot.
